findings.claim: The philosopher David Hume called this the “inconsistent triad” — the three ideas seem to contradict each other. (repeated in flashcard 9 “Which philosopher named the omnipotent–loving–just tension the 'inconsistent triad'?” → “David Hume.” and in the 12-mark mark scheme bullet “David Hume’s inconsistent triad”)
findings.truth: Hume never used the phrase. In Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion (published 1779) he restates Epicurus's questions about God's power, goodness and the existence of evil. The label 'inconsistent triad' belongs to the modern discussion of the logical problem of evil, associated with J. L. Mackie's 'Evil and Omnipotence' (1955). Keep Hume as the philosopher a GCSE student names, but drop the false coinage.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Problem of evil (Hume quoting Epicurus; no coinage credited to Hume); Wikipedia, J. L. Mackie ('Evil and Omnipotence', 1955)

findings.claim: Question 2: “Name the three persons of the Trinity.” typed “1 mark — Give/Name”, mark note “[1 mark for all three named correctly]”
findings.truth: Each five-part question is worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks, and both short questions are single-point recall. A 1-mark question that only credits three correct items misrepresents the paper and tells a student the wrong amount of writing. Lessons 3 and 4 already use the correct single-point form.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 and 4.4.1 — 'two five-part questions of 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks'

findings.claim: 12-mark mark scheme: “Max Level 2 if no reference to religion” plus band descriptors copied in board style (“Well-argued response with reasoned consideration of different points of view. Logical chains of reasoning supported by knowledge. References to religion applied to the issue.”)
findings.truth: ‘Level 2’ is a banned band name and the descriptors reproduce board mark-scheme wording. The ceiling itself is right (an answer with no religious content cannot pass the 4-6 band); it must be stated in house wording.

findings.claim: “he sits ‘at the right hand of God’ (the Nicene Creed)”, repeated in flashcard 13 “According to the Nicene Creed, where does the ascended Jesus sit?” → “At the right hand of God”
findings.truth: The Nicene Creed reads 'and is seated at the right hand of the Father'. 'At the right hand of God' is the Apostles' Creed phrasing ('at the right hand of God the Father almighty'). A student quoting the Nicene Creed must write 'the Father'.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Nicene Creed — 'sits on the right hand of the Father' in the 1662 and modern English translations

findings.claim: “Simply describing a belief without a source will limit you to a maximum of 4 marks.”
findings.truth: The spec fixes the question at 6 marks and says the first four parts test AO1, but it does not publish the split. The lesson's own mark scheme uses 2 + 2 + 2 (two beliefs plus the source), which makes the 4-mark ceiling correct. Options: (a) keep it, because it matches the scheme printed in the same lesson; (b) soften to 'you will lose the marks reserved for the source'. Recommendation: keep it — it is internally consistent and it tells the student the right thing to do.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 and 4.4.1 (marks 1, 1, 4, 6, 12; AO1 in the first four parts); lesson 2 practice question 4 mark scheme
findings.ruling: Leave (matches printed scheme / corpus-wide relabel queue).

findings.claim: Atonement collapsible: “This view is associated with Anselm of Canterbury and is the foundational Catholic/Thomistic atonement model. Note: the penal substitution view described above is a distinctly Protestant teaching, rooted in Luther and Calvin; Anselm's satisfaction theory differs in mechanism (paying an honour-debt, not a penal penalty).”
findings.truth: The theology is right, but the 'Note:' reads as an editor's aside to a teacher and uses vocabulary well above age 15-16 ('Thomistic', 'penal penalty', 'honour-debt'). Worth rewriting for the student on a later content pass; no factual correction needed.

summary: Scripture is sound: every verse in the unit (Luke 1:37, John 3:16, 2 Thessalonians 1:6, Jeremiah 1:5, Genesis 1:1-3, John 1:1-3, 1 Corinthians 15:17, Luke 23:43, Matthew 25:31-46, John 1:14, Matthew 3:17, Mark 9:7, Luke 22:42, Matthew 28:6, John 11:25, Acts 1:9, Romans 3:23, Romans 5:8, Ephesians 2:8-9, James 2:17, John 14:26, Isaiah 53:5) is verbatim NIV with the right book, chapter and verse, and every knowledge-check answer key and match order is correct. The real problems are a misattributed coinage (Hume and the 'inconsistent triad'), a Nicene Creed clause quoted as 'right hand of God' instead of 'right hand of the Father', two 1-mark practice questions that demand two or three correct items, and banned board band names left in four mark schemes and one exam tip.
